rules.statement: Never let a test project (or its Directory.Build.props) set TreatWarningsAsErrors back to false; test projects stay under the same zero-warning gate as every other project.
rules.why: The gate covers all code the family maintains, not just code it ships; xUnit analyzers report real defects in tests, and warnings that pile up under an exemption go unread and hide the next real one.
rules.check: Look for TreatWarningsAsErrors=false, removed WarningsAsErrors, or similar opt-outs in test project files or tests/Directory.Build.props.

rules.statement: Resolve a warning by fixing the code first, for example with a nullable local for a [MaybeNullWhen(false)] out argument, Assert.NotNull before a dereference, or a specific exception type instead of new Exception(…). Only then add a per-rule .editorconfig entry with a one-line reason. As a last resort, use a tight #pragma warning disable/restore pair with a reason at a single site.
rules.why: Fixing the code is the default remedy. Suppressions are justified exceptions that must be narrow and explained.
rules.check: Look for new suppressions (pragma, SuppressMessage, editorconfig severity changes, NoWarn) where a code fix was possible. Also look for a pragma disable without a matching restore, a pragma that covers more than the one site, or a suppression with no reason.

rules.statement: Turn an analyzer rule off for test files only when it is legitimate on shipping code but noise in tests, scope it to the test-files .editorconfig block, and record its reason beside the entry. Never disable rules wholesale for tests.
rules.why: A reader then sees each exception and its cause together, and suppressing whole rule sets instead of fixing code was rejected.
rules.check: In a diff to .editorconfig, look for new severity=none entries for tests that have no one-line reason comment, that are scoped beyond the test glob, or that are broad category-wide suppressions.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't flag per-test JsonSerializerOptions instances (CA1869), Method_State_Expected underscore test names (CA1707), collaborators held through their interface (CA1859), inline array literals passed to assertion helpers (CA1861), or test base classes without a finalizer (CA1816).
rules.why: These rules are deliberately off for tests. JsonSerializerOptions becomes immutable on first use, so each test builds its own for isolation, and caching doesn't matter in a test. The other four are test idioms.
rules.check: Before reporting one of these patterns, confirm the file is test code covered by the test-files .editorconfig block.

rules.statement: In shipping code, don't use the legacy JwtSecurityTokenHandler or JwtSecurityToken types.
rules.why: These legacy types have no place in shipping code and are banned through the family's BannedSymbols.txt.
rules.check: Look for references to System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt.JwtSecurityTokenHandler or JwtSecurityToken in packable projects.

rules.statement: In shipping code, don't convert untrusted numeric dates with the throwing DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds or FromUnixTimeMilliseconds. Use a non-throwing, range-checked numeric-date conversion instead.
rules.why: The throwing conversions are banned in shipping code, and the family provides non-throwing coercion helpers to use in their place.
rules.check: Look for DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds/FromUnixTimeMilliseconds calls in packable projects.

rules.statement: Don't report a test project for referencing types that are banned in shipping code, such as the legacy JWT handler or a third-party JOSE library, when the test uses them as an independent cross-validation oracle. Don't ask for a suppression for such a reference either.
rules.why: Tests use independent implementations as oracles, and banning them would defeat the cross-validation strategy. The shipping-code banned list is intentionally not applied to test projects. The strict-encoding banned list still binds tests.
rules.check: Confirm the file is in a test project and the banned type serves as a reference implementation that production output is checked against. Still flag banned strict-encoding APIs in tests.

rules.statement: Don't flag a test project for setting GenerateDocumentationFile to true while suppressing CS1591.
rules.why: Roslyn evaluates IDE0005 (unused usings) only when documentation generation is on, and hard-errors if the rule is raised while it is off. The XML is discarded because test assemblies are never packed.
rules.check: Before reporting documentation settings in test Directory.Build.props or csproj files, check whether IDE0005 is raised as a warning.

rules.statement: Don't ask a test project or other non-packable project to add PublicAPI.Shipped/Unshipped tracking or to satisfy PublicApiAnalyzers diagnostics.
rules.why: PublicApiAnalyzers run only where IsPackable is not false, because test assemblies have no tracked public surface.
rules.check: Check IsPackable for the project before reporting missing public API tracking.
